correctness.rationale: At a prescribed target the cubic ψ(w)=w−w³/6 increases onto [0,5/6), so the permitted third-coordinate lifts are exactly W+k with 0≤k<5A/6−W; the strict upper inequality gives the stated ceiling, even at a seam. For each w, writing mv=δ+j exhausts the second coordinate with j=0,…,m−1. If mv>0 the allowed positive first-coordinate lift lies in (0,δ+j]; it has j integer translates of U−w plus one iff 0<{U−w}≤δ. This checks both half-open boundaries. For mv=0 the first coordinate forces w=U, and the remaining equations give exactly Γ_m, with every u allowed; at most one w-sheet contributes such an interval. For example at m=1 the target (1/2,1/2,0) has exactly the solution (0,1/2,0), (0,1/2,0) as a target has no preimage, (0,0,5/6) excludes the third-coordinate endpoint, and (0,0,0) has the whole v=w=0 interval. On fixed smooth lifts, subtracting the differential terms through U and V gives determinant −m²vA(1−w²/2); this is not a differentiability assertion at modular seams. For m≥2 at least one sheet exists and its baseline count is positive away from Γ_m. For m=1 the given unreachable target also follows from the cubic range. For m=64, 64≤A<66 gives 53≤s≤55 and per-sheet counts between 2016 and 2080, so the two numerical bounds are valid; the record expressly does not claim sharp extrema. The proof is exact, not based on the finite floating-point reconstructions in the supplied script, which was inspected but not executed.
